introduction_transcription.expected: At each redshift, a photon budget can look open because galaxies leak too little ionizing light, or because model assumptions carry the mismatch. If galaxies were genuinely leaking too little ionizing radiation, that would limit how they could maintain reionization. But an apparent shortfall could instead be a fact about low-redshift proxy transport or another frozen assumption, not about the galaxies. How do we tell a source shortfall from an assumption shortfall?
